english.title: Disclose information relating to free school lunches
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) disclosed information relating to **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) which you had received by virtue of section

(A)_[110(3)]_
(B)_[110(4)]_
(C)_[110(5)]_

of the Education Act 2005 other than as permitted by section 111(1) of that Act
english.legislation: Contrary to section 111(1) and (4) of the Education Act 2005.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
disclosed information received
by virtue of s 110(3) / (5)
which related to a particular person

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: An offence is not committed if the information is received by virtue of subsection (3) in accordance with subsection (5) OR in the course of any duty he has in connection with the exercise of functions relating to eligibility for free school lunches and milk OR in accordance with an enactment or an order of a court OR with consent. It is a defence if he reasonably believed his disclosure was lawful.

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Note:
In relation to an offence committed before paragraph 24(2) of Schedule 22 to the Sentencing Act 2020 comes into force (01/12/20), the reference to 12 months imprisonment in relation to summary offences, above, is to be read as a reference to 6 months imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
